title: Tear Gas / Pepper Spray
subtitle: Immediate Response & Recovery
content:
Source: Physicians for Human Rights

WHAT TO DO IMMEDIATELY

• Get out of the cloud of tear gas and away from the affected area as quickly as possible. If possible, seek higher ground.

• Walk, don't run. Running causes heavier breathing, increasing tear gas inhalation.

• If your eyes are burning or your vision is blurry, flush them immediately with clean, cool water for 10–15 minutes.

• Avoid touching your eyes, nose, or mouth.

• If water is unavailable, avoid using baby wipes or makeup wipes as they may increase irritation.

• There is no evidence that milk or baking soda works better than cool water.

• If you are unaffected, help move others to a clean, well-ventilated area.

• Never attempt to pick up or remove tear gas canisters.

────────────────────

BEFORE ATTENDING A PROTEST

Wear:

• A face mask, scarf, or bandana covering your nose and mouth.

• Shatter-resistant eye protection (goggles or safety glasses).

• Clothing that covers as much skin as possible.

• Comfortable closed-toe shoes suitable for running.

Avoid:

• Contact lenses.

• Makeup, especially around the eyes.

────────────────────

WHAT TO BRING

• Water bottle with a squeeze top (for drinking and flushing eyes).

• Backpack or drawstring bag.

• Identification and emergency contact information.

• Cash for transport or emergency situations.

• Prescription medication, inhalers, or EpiPens.

• Medical alert information if applicable.

• A spare change of clothes.

────────────────────

AFTER EXPOSURE

• Change contaminated clothing as soon as possible.

• Leave shoes outside before entering your home.

• Air contaminated clothing outdoors for at least 48 hours or seal it in a plastic bag until it can be washed separately.

• Do not wash contaminated clothing with clean clothes.

• Take a cold shower for at least 20 minutes and wash your hair thoroughly.

• Keep your eyes closed as much as possible while showering.

• If symptoms persist for more than 30 minutes, or you develop breathing problems, vision changes, severe pain, or other concerning symptoms, seek medical attention immediately.

title: Bleeding
subtitle: Control Blood Loss
content: Apply firm, direct pressure with a clean cloth or bandage. Elevate the injured area if possible. Call emergency services if bleeding is severe or cannot be controlled.

title: Head Injury
subtitle: Possible Concussion
content: If the person loses consciousness, vomits repeatedly, has seizures, severe headache, confusion, or unequal pupils, seek emergency medical care immediately.

title: Fractures
subtitle: Broken Bones
content: Do not try to straighten the limb. Immobilize it in the position found. Apply ice wrapped in cloth if available and seek medical care.

title: Heat Exhaustion
subtitle: High Temperatures
content: Move to shade, loosen clothing, drink water slowly, and cool the body with wet cloths. If confusion or unconsciousness develops, call emergency services.

title: CPR
subtitle: Cardiac Emergency
content: If someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally, call emergency services immediately. Begin chest compressions if trained.
